subject: Concord Systems – capacity concordance & GPU mix recommendation
body_preview: Recommending a mixed fleet: H100 for infrequent long-context workloads, A100 as steady reserve, and L4 for burst/low-cost low-latency traffic. See attached matrix and MOP.
messages:
From: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@concordsys.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@concordsys.com, ml-team@concordsys.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity guidance request — long-context chat assistant

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Concord's execs liked the latency numbers. We're heading into procurement and need a clear recommendation from Redwood for Dedicated capacity sizing tied to the upcoming contract. High-level:

- Production workload: multi-turn chat assistant with ~10–20k token context for a subset (~5%) of requests; most requests are 256–1024 tokens.
- Expected steady QPS: 120 concurrent inference requests (peaks 250) with average session length ~30s; token mix skewed (long-tail).
- Latency SLO: 95th < 450ms for typical 1k-token requests, long-context can be 1.2–1.8s acceptable for 10–20k token runs.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement is asking for a recommended GPU SKU mix and a short rationale (H100 vs A100 vs L4), plus a 30/90-day pilot plan and deliverables for handoff to ops.

Can you send a recommended initial SKU split (reserve vs burst) and an ops playbook we can include in the SOW? Procurement also asked for an attachment outlining memory headroom assumptions.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — can we get something by EOD Monday?

Alex
Alex Monroe
Head of ML Engineering, Concord Systems
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@concordsys.com>
Cc: procurement@concordsys.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guidance request — long-context chat assistant

Alex — thanks for the context and the clear ask. I put together an initial recommendation and an attached decision matrix (concord-capacity-concordance-matrix.xlsx) that maps expected token profiles to SKU choices and memory margins. High level summary below and the MOP PDF contains the handoff checklist.

Summary recommendation (pilot phase — 30 days):
- Reserve pool (baseline): 60% A100 (balanced memory/perf), 25% H100 (memory-heavy long-context runs), 15% L4 (low-cost inference for short requests).
- Burst layer: allow autoscale to L4-backed nodes for transient QPS spikes; L4 absorbs short low-latency sessions to reduce A100/H100 contention.
- Memory headroom: for 20k-token worst-case, allocate H100 nodes with >=100GB effective model memory (use sharding/quantization as detailed in the attachment).
- Fallback policy: prefer streaming + prefix KV caching for long-context to reduce memory pressure; if H100 slots are saturated, degrade to A100 with reduced batch concurrency (different SLO).

Deliverables we propose for SOW: capacity matrix (attached), 30-day pilot runbook (metrics + regression gates), and a 90-day scale plan with SKU rebalancing checkpoints.

If that aligns, I'll pull Karthik in for the micro-architecture tradeoffs (quant, KV cache sizing, eviction behavior) and we can schedule a technical sync Monday.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Deal Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachments: concord-capacity-concordance-matrix.xlsx, redwood-mop-concord-summary.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: (internal)
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: internal: technical notes for Concord SKU split (H100/A100/L4)

Naomi / Irene — quick technical addendum to the matrix before we finalize for Concord. Key tradeoffs and numbers to justify the proposed 60/25/15 reserve mix:

1) Workload profile mapping
   - Long-context (10–20k tokens): memory-bound, low concurrency (~5–10 qps). H100 provides the local memory capacity for single-shot long sequences and reduces cross-node sharding complexity.
   - Mid-range (1k tokens): mixed memory/compute; A100 handles steady throughput with predictable latency. Good for the bulk of traffic.
   - Short (<512 tokens): latency-first cheap inference; L4 is cost-effective and supports high QPS with lower per-token cost.

2) Quantization and memory optimization
   - Recommend 8-bit PTQ for A100 and L4 where possible; for H100 long-context runs we prefer 4-bit quant + grouped-quant kernels only if we validate output quality for Concord's LLM.
   - KV cache strategy: keep prefix-only cache on H100; stream large contexts in windows to bound memory. Eviction policy: LRU per-session with small write-back window.

3) Concurrency assumptions (numbers to put into SOW)
   - Baseline reserve sizing: support 120 steady concurrent sessions with headroom 1.5x; reserve nodes sized to 180 concurrent equivalent. This maps to the 60/25/15 ratio at expected token lengths.
   - Burst policy: autoscale target to handle 250 peak concurrency; route burst to L4 first (cheap) and only use overflow A100/H100 when sustained >5m.

4) Operational knobs and monitoring
   - Track per-model KV memory usage, OOM incidence, average token latency by SKU, and cold-start penalty.
   - Instrument fallback metric: percentage of long-context requests that had to be downgraded to A100. Set a threshold (initially 5%) to trigger SKU rebalance.

5) Risk and mitigation
   - Risk: long-context correctness regressions with aggressive 4-bit quant. Mitigation: canary quantized model on a subset (5%) of long-context sessions.

If that reads OK I'll incorporate exact node-counts into the spreadsheet and Naomi can send the customer-facing version.

—Karthik
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guidance request — long-context chat assistant

Alex — thanks for the patience. Attached is the customer-facing capacity concordance matrix and our MOP summary (see attachments). TL;DR: we recommend starting with the pilot SKU split below and gate scaling decisions on the pilot's telemetry.

Pilot SKU split (reserve pool):
- A100: 60% — steady-state workhorse for 1k-token profile
- H100: 25% — reserved for long-context runs (10–20k tokens) and heavy KV cache slots
- L4: 15% — low-cost, low-latency pool for short requests and burst absorption

Operational plan highlights:
- Pilot length: 30 days (success gate: meet latency SLOs on baseline traffic and <5% long-context downgrades)
- Metrics we will provide daily: per-SKU p95/p99 latency, per-request token counts, KV cache hit rate, OOM counts, and cost run-rate.
- Next steps: procurement sign-off on the attached matrix, DocuSign for SOW (we'll circulate), technical kickoff (we suggest Mon 2026-06-07 10:00 PT).

Attachments: concord-capacity-concordance-matrix.xlsx, redwood-mop-concord-summary.pdf

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
